rv.q: Instead, you admire the production for its sometimes brilliant ideas.

Despite this, the attitudes of society remain unwavering in their disdain of Anna, and in the place of women within a male-dominated world. An omnipresent three-piece orchestra creates a quite brilliant soundscape of underscoring and romanticism alongside a discordant array of Hitchcock-like horror sounds composed by Paddy Cunneen.
Natalie Dormer stars in this cumbersome, intermittently arresting adaptation of the Tolstoy classic
Overall, I feel it was perhaps too broad of a take on this interesting story, as we lose the drive of our protagonist at times.
